title: Keeper guidelines for component lifecycle and retirement playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose:
Create a single, pragmatic "keeper" playbook that clarifies how designers contribute to and retire design system artifacts (tokens, buttons, tables, charts). This doc reduces ad-hoc decisions, speeds reviews, and standardizes migration paths for consumers across Redwood products.

Scope:
- Contribution: intake, required artifacts (Figma components, token files, usage examples), automated checks, and who signs off.
- Review checklist: visual, accessibility, API surface (props/variants), responsive behaviour, and migration notes.
- RFC process: when to open, template, reviewers, approval thresholds, and expected timeline.
- Deprecation policy: notice periods, communication cadence, automated codemods where possible, and sunset gating.
- Maintenance roles: Keepers (owners), Stewards (wider reviewers), and Consumers (teams that rely on components).

High-level principles:
1) Backward compatibility first: prefer additive changes; breaking changes require an RFC and deprecation warning.
2) Shippable artefacts: every PR must include design tokens, Figma updates, and a migration note for consumers.
3) Clear ownership: each component/token has a Keeper listed in the registry; Keepers are responsible for roadmap and deprecation decisions.

Contribution flow (short):
1. Intake: open issue in Design board with prototype link and problem statement.
2. RFC: for any surface/API change or token rename, open an RFC (use template) and tag Keepers + ENG.
3. Design PR: include Figma file, release notes draft, suggested codemod (if breaking), and test plan.
4. Review: 3 reviewers minimum (Keeper, Accessibility reviewer, Eng reviewer).
5. Merge & rollout: schedule canary, add console observability note if high-traffic.

Review checklist (to paste into PR):
- Visual: pixel alignment, spacing tokens used correctly, cross-platform parity.
- Tokens: do new tokens follow naming conventions? Are aliases documented?
- Accessibility: keyboard navigation, focus states, color contrast, ARIA.
- API/Props: minimal props, clear defaults, prop deprecation annotated.
- Performance: does component render cheaply? Any large bundle-size regressions?
- Docs: examples for primary permutations and migration guide.
- Testing: visual snapshot, accessibility audit, unit tests for behaviour.

RFC process (operational):
- Template fields: motivation, alternatives considered, migration plan, rollout plan, concerns and metrics to monitor.
- Review window: 7 business days default; P0 changes require expedited 48-hour review cycle.
- Approval: either Keeper + ENG reviewer or 2 Keepers if cross-team; record decision and link RFC to release notes.

Deprecation policy (concrete):
- Minor cosmetic changes: no deprecation required if additive.
- Token renames/semantic changes: 90-day deprecation window with explicit aliasing for token synonyms.
- Component API break: 180-day deprecation window + codemod + migration guide + deprecation banner in docs.
- Hard removal: only after previously announced window and cross-team sign-off from Product and Eng.

Migration & tooling:
- Codemod standard template in repo: authors must supply a codemod for any API break with >2 known consumers.
- Automated lint rule: disallow usage of flagged-deprecated tokens/components; run in CI to catch regressions.
- Registry update: Keeper must update the component registry entry (owner, use-cases, migration links).

Communication & rollout:
- Announcement channels: #design-system, weekly public changelog, and release bulletin for major changes.
- Consumer outreach: identify top 5 internal consumers and invite to migration plan reviews.
- Telemetry: tag releases with metrics to monitor adoption and errors for one release cycle.

Decision rationale & trade-offs:
- 180-day windows balance speed of iteration with developer churn; shorter windows increase rework.
- Requiring codemods increases initial work but materially lowers migration friction for large teams.
- Keeper model centralizes fast decisions but requires rotation policy to avoid single-person bottlenecks.

Examples (illustrative timelines):
- Token aliasing: rename token -- announce + alias for 90 days -> deprecate alias -> remove after 6 months.
- Button prop rename: open RFC -> 180-day deprecation -> provide codemod -> monitor adoption -> remove.

Deliverables for this ticket:
- Final playbook doc (Confluence) with copy + checklists.
- PR template updates and RFC template in the design repo.
- Lint rule PR and codemod skeleton examples.
- Keeper roster CSV uploaded to shared Drive.

Links to artifacts (work-in-progress):
- Figma draft: https://www.figma.com/file/REDWOOD/keeper-playbook-draft
- RFC template: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/DS/RFC+Template
- Draft Confluence page: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/DS/Keeper+Playbook+Draft
- Codemod examples repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-codemods

Metrics of success:
- 50% reduction in unplanned design churn in two sprints measured via changelog rollbacks.
- >90% PRs include required checklist items within first two weeks after rollout.
- Consumer satisfaction score >4/5 on migration experience survey.
